learning_outcomes.text: Familiarize with analytical solution techniques for some first-order ordinary equations.
Familiarize with solution techniques for higher-order linear equations and linear systems.
Understand basic qualitative analysis techniques for solutions of first-order equations and two-dimensional linear systems.
Know basic types of boundary problems as a basis for the study of partial differential equations.
Gain knowledge of numerical solution methods for differential equations.
Develop skills in using Matlab software and programming numerical methods.

assessment_methods.method: Main examination (final exam or two partials)

assessment_rules: The final grade is a weighted sum of a main examination component (75%), computer practices (20%), and tutorials (5%). Students can opt for a single final exam counting for 75% of the grade, or two partial exams each counting for 37.5% of the grade. A minimum grade of 3.5 in the final exam (or 3 in the second partial if chosen) is required for averaging. For extraordinary sittings, the final grade is a weighted sum of the final exam (80%) and computer practices (20%), with a minimum grade of 3.5 in the final exam required for averaging.
